faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella in June 2038?
faq.a: June in Marbella averages 28°C air temperature, 22°C sea temperature, and 11 hours of sunshine daily. Winds are light easterly at 10–15 knots, making for calm cruising conditions. Rain is rare – typically only 2–3 days in the month.

faq.q: When should I book a boat rental for June 2038?
faq.a: Book 4 to 6 weeks in advance. June is peak season, and our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) often sell out by mid-month. Tier B boats like the Mangusta 80 require a 4-hour minimum and have limited availability – early booking secures your preferred vessel.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a group of 10 in June?
faq.a: For 10 guests, the Azimut 39 (11 pax) or Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax) are ideal. Both depart from Puerto Banús and include a skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks. The Azimut 39 is €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full day.

faq.q: Can I swim or use a jet ski during the charter?
faq.a: Yes. All charters allow swimming stops at spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. The Mangusta 80 (Tier B) includes a free jet ski for the duration. Other boats can arrange jet ski hire on request – contact us via WhatsApp for pricing.

faq.q: What is included in the rental price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). No hidden extras – just bring sunscreen and swimwear.

faq.q: Are there any restrictions for June charters?
faq.a: Maximum 12 guests per boat (except Dubhe and Mariah SX21 which take 5). No pets allowed. All guests must carry ID. Skipper has final say on itinerary based on weather. No loud music after sunset in port.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on my booking day?
faq.a: We monitor forecasts closely. If conditions are unsafe (e.g. high winds over 30 knots or thunderstorms), we offer a full refund or reschedule to an alternative date. Typically June has very stable weather – cancellations are rare.

faq.q: Can I charter a boat for a half-day in June?
faq.a: Yes. Half-day options are 2, 3, or 4 hours. Tier A boats start at €749 for 2 hours. For a longer experience, 8-hour full-day charters are available from €2,299. All include the same inclusions regardless of duration.

data.body_html:
June 2038 in Marbella delivers near-perfect conditions for a day on the water: 28°C air temperature, 22°C sea temperature, and 11 hours of sunshine. Whether you're planning a family outing or a celebration with friends, a Marbella boat rental from Puerto Banús is the smartest way to beat the heat and see the coast. This guide covers what to expect weather-wise, how to book smart during peak season, and which boats suit your group size.

June 2038 Weather Averages for Marbella

June marks the start of high summer on the Costa del Sol. Expect clear skies, light easterly winds (10–15 knots), and minimal rain – typically just 2–3 days of precipitation across the month. Humidity is low, around 55%, so it feels comfortable even at midday. Sea breezes keep the coast cooler than inland areas. For boaters, this means calm seas and excellent visibility for spotting dolphins or the silhouette of La Concha mountain.

  • Average high: 28°C (82°F)
  • Average low: 19°C (66°F)
  • Sea temperature: 22°C (72°F)
  • Sunshine: 11 hours per day
  • Rainfall: 5 mm total
  • Wind: 10–15 knots, east-northeast

Peak Season Booking Tips for June 2038

June is peak season in Marbella. Puerto Banús marinas fill up fast, and our most popular boats – the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 – are often booked weeks ahead. To secure your preferred vessel, book 4–6 weeks in advance. Tier B boats like the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) require a minimum 4-hour charter at €4,719, which includes a free jet ski. For larger groups, consider splitting into two boats: e.g., a Mangusta 80 plus a Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) – contact us via WhatsApp for custom quotes.

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús. Here's a quick overview of what's available – pricing is fixed for Tier A and Tier B; other boats are on request.

Best Itineraries for June Days

With long daylight hours, you have time to explore. A popular route from Puerto Banús heads east to Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés – two rocky coves with crystal-clear water ideal for swimming. Alternatively, head west towards Estepona (25 minutes by speedboat) or further to Sotogrande (45 minutes). For a shorter trip, circle the Marbella coastline past the Golden Mile and Cabopino beach. Your skipper will tailor the route to your preferences.

What to Pack for a June Charter

Pack light: swimwear, a towel, sunglasses, a hat, and high-SPF sunscreen (the reflection off the water amplifies UV). A light jacket or long-sleeve shirt is useful for the return trip when the sea breeze picks up. All boats have shaded areas and a fresh-water shower. Don't forget your camera – the views of La Concha and the Sierra Blanca are stunning in the June light.
